newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's health insurance plan worries workers.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's health insurance plan worries workers.

text.p: Kuwait's plan to make foreign residents pay a health insurance fee could fail unless employers shoulder the cost, economists and diplomats said on Wednesday.
The government wants to impose a mandatory annual health insurance fee of about 50 dinars ($164) on foreign workers and their dependants, totalling 1.25 million people.
About 500,000 foreign workers earn 400-700 dinars a year, say economists and diplomats.
"If labourers were asked to pay the fee on their own, it would be simply impossible" to implement the measure, said leading Kuwaiti economist Jassem al-Saadoun.
The envisaged fee, which covers services by state-run hospitals only, would rise gradually to about 150 dinars a year over a five-year-span, insurance industry sources said.

Officials have said the plan, which needs parliament's approval, does not require employers to pay the fee, while another plan that would apply to nationals includes terms obliging the state and employers to contribute.
But, many employers would probably deduct the fees back from their workers if they were obliged to pay, a diplomat said.
"I will send my wife and four children to live with my mother in Cairo," said Bioumi, 43, an Egyptian accountant.
"Either that or I'll have to steal," added Bioumi who earns 300 dinars a month. "My salary will not be enough for food."
Oil-rich Kuwait, which has a native population of about 720,000 people, depends largely on foreign workers mainly from Asian and other Arab countries.

The state, which currently provides health care services virtually free of charge for a population totalling two million people at an annual cost of about 270 million dinars, also heavily subsidises electricity, water, petrol and some foods.
The state budget deficit is projected at about 1.274 billion dinars for the current fiscal year (July-June).
